title: Fog Watch: Temperature and Dew Point Convergence
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Six overnight traces. Commit to dew, frost, fog or nothing at 22:00, then watch the rest of the night. One scenario is built so that relative humidity lies to you.

educational.topic: Fog Watch: Temperature and Dew Point Convergence
learningObjectives: Predict overnight dew, frost or fog from the converging gap between air temperature and dew point.
Justify the prediction from cooling rate and sky conditions rather than from relative humidity alone.

keyQuestions: What does a spread of two degrees at midnight tell you?
Why can a clear calm night produce dew but not fog?
Relative humidity is 85 per cent. Is fog likely?
commonMisconceptions: Reading high relative humidity as an imminent fog warning.
Assuming a converging spread always finishes converging.
Treating frost as frozen dew rather than as direct deposition.
assessmentOpportunities: Predicts overnight condensation from the spread and its rate of closing.
Names wind and cloud as reasons a converging spread may not finish.
Explains why relative humidity alone is insufficient for this forecast.
